subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should `read` fail loud for known binary document formats now, or should this issue wait for broader parser/native-document support?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the issue mixes a small safe fallback with parser/native document behavior that changes security and ownership boundaries.

options.title: Ship safe read guard
options.body: Add MIME/extension detection for known binary documents and return a concise unsupported-file message that points users to dedicated document tools where available.

options.title: Adopt or replace fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source work only after review, then land a current-main target-repo patch or close the fork PR as obsolete.

options.title: Wait for document architecture
options.body: Defer `read` behavior until the broader document extraction and provider-native file-input issues define the permanent policy.

recommendation.title: Ship safe read guard
recommendation.body: Add MIME/extension detection for known binary documents and return a concise unsupported-file message that points users to dedicated document tools where available.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mostly product boundary and document/tool ownership, and steipete has the clearest adjacent media/input-file routing history from the inspected commits.
